# Temple Scroll Column 56 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** 11Q19 (Cave 11), Col. 56 | **Condition:** well preserved

---

**56:1** You shall not muzzle an ox in its threshing.

**56:2** When brothers dwell together and one of them dies and a son is not to him, the wife of the dead-one shall not be to the outside, to a strange man; her brother-in-law shall go in to her and take her to himself for a wife and perform-the-duty-of-a-brother-in-law to her.

**56:3** And it shall be, the firstborn whom she bears shall arise upon the name of his dead brother, and his name shall not be wiped out from Israel.

**56:4** And if the man does not desire to take his sister-in-law, then his sister-in-law shall go up to the gate, to the elders, and say: My brother-in-law refuses to raise up for his brother a name in Israel; he is not willing to perform-the-duty-of-a-brother-in-law to me.

**56:5** And the elders of his city shall call him and speak to him; and he shall stand and say: I do not desire to take her.

**56:6** Then his sister-in-law shall draw near to him before the eyes of the elders and pull his sandal from upon his foot and spit in his face, and she shall answer and say: Thus shall it be done to the man who does not build up the house of his brother.

**56:7** And his name shall be called in Israel: The House of the One-Whose-Sandal-Was-Pulled-Off.

**56:8** When men struggle together, a man and his brother, and the wife of the one draws near to deliver her husband from the hand of the one striking him, and she stretches out her hand and seizes his shameful-parts —

**56:9** then you shall cut off her hand; your eye shall not show-pity.

**56:10** You shall not have in your bag a stone and a stone, a great and a small.

**56:11** You shall not have in your house an ephah and an ephah, a great and a small.

**56:12** A whole and righteous stone you shall have; a whole and righteous ephah you shall have, so that your days may be lengthened upon the land which the LORD your God is giving to you.

**56:13** For an abomination of the LORD your God is everyone doing these things, everyone doing unrighteousness.

**56:14** When you come into the land which I am giving to you, and you possess it and dwell in it, and you say: I will set over me a king like all the nations which are around me —

**56:15** setting, you shall set over you a king whom I shall choose; from the midst of your brothers you shall set over you a king; you are not able to set over you a foreign man who is not your brother.

**56:16** Only he shall not multiply to himself horses, and he shall not return the people to Egypt in order to multiply horses, for I have said to you: You shall not return again by this way.

**56:17** And he shall not multiply to himself wives, and his heart shall not turn aside; and silver and gold he shall not multiply to himself greatly.

**56:18** And it shall be, when he sits upon the throne of his kingdom, they shall write for him a copy of this Torah upon a scroll, from before the priests.

**56:19** And it shall be with him, and he shall read in it all the days of his life, so that he may learn to fear the LORD his God, to keep all the words of this Torah and these statutes, to do them,

**56:20** so that his heart is not lifted up above his brothers, and so that he does not turn aside from the commandment to the right or to the left, so that he may lengthen days upon his kingdom, he and his sons, in the midst of Israel.

**56:21** And he shall not [...] the inheritance of any tribe, for each shall hold to his inheritance.

---

*EMET notes: Column 56 reworks Deuteronomy 25:4-17:20, transitioning from miscellaneous laws to the Law of the King. "Perform-the-duty-of-a-brother-in-law" (yibbem) preserved as compound to mark the technical levirate term. "Shameful-parts" (mevushav) rendered euphemistically per Hebrew. The Law of the King begins at 56:14 with the characteristic first-person divine voice — "whom I shall choose."*
